summary:
This is printed page 618 of the index (PDF 642). The left column finishes the **R** entries (RetinaNet detector, return_sequences argument, RLHF, RMSE, RNNs, RoBERTa, ROC AUC) and the rest of the page covers **S** from *sample or input* to *stateless_call() method*.

**How to use it:** every number is a *printed* page number. To open the right PDF page, add 24 (e.g. printed 364 is PDF 388).

**Main clusters on this page**

- **Recurrent networks (chapter 13):** *RNNs* 352, 364–378 (PDF 376, 388–402), with sub-entries for the overview (365–367 → PDF 389–391), recurrent layers in Keras (368–372 → PDF 392–396), recurrent dropout (373–375 → PDF 397–399), stacking recurrent layers (375 → PDF 399) and bidirectional RNNs (377–378 → PDF 401–402). *SimpleRNN layer* 369 (PDF 393) and *return_sequences argument* 368 (PDF 392) belong here too.
- **Sequence-to-sequence learning (chapter 15):** *seq2seq* 428–437 (PDF 452–461), English-to-Spanish translation 430–432 (PDF 454–456), with RNNs 433–437 (PDF 457–461), with a Transformer 449 (PDF 473); *self-attention* 444 (PDF 468); *Shakespeare language model* 422–428 (PDF 446–452).
- **LLMs and generative models:** *RLHF* 495–498 (PDF 519–522), *Stable Diffusion* 531 (PDF 555), *slerp / spherical linear interpolation* 535 (PDF 559).
- **Vision:** *RetinaNet detector* 347–349 (PDF 371–373), *SAM (Segment Anything Model)* 319 (PDF 343), *semantic segmentation* 310 (PDF 334), *SSD* and *single-stage detectors* 332 (PDF 356), *separable convolution* 269 (PDF 293).
- **Fundamentals:** *softmax activation* 119, 126, 440, 601 (PDF 143, 150, 464, 625), *sigmoid activation* 245, 601 (PDF 269, 625), *sparse_categorical_crossentropy* 124 (PDF 148), *simple hold-out validation* 150 (PDF 174), *shallow learning* 7 (PDF 31).
- **Chapter 19's outlook:** *search* 584–594 (PDF 608–618), with sub-entries on the two poles of abstraction, program synthesis and blending deep learning with program synthesis.

concepts.name: RNNs (recurrent neural networks)
concepts.intuition: An RNN processes a sequence one step at a time and carries a state from step to step.
concepts.technical: Sub-entries: overview 365–367 (PDF 389–391), recurrent layers in Keras 368–372 (PDF 392–396), recurrent dropout 373–375 (PDF 397–399), stacking 375 (PDF 399), bidirectional 377–378 (PDF 401–402), seq2seq with RNNs 433–437 (PDF 457–461).
concepts.significance: The main treatment is in chapter 13 (timeseries forecasting), starting at PDF 388.
concepts.example: To read about SimpleRNN, use the separate entry 'SimpleRNN layer 369' → PDF 393.
concepts.misconception: The page numbers are printed numbers, not PDF numbers; 364 printed is PDF 388.

concepts.name: seq2seq (sequence-to-sequence) learning
concepts.definition: Index entry: printed 428–437 → PDF 452–461; with Transformer 449 → PDF 473.
concepts.intuition: Mapping one sequence (e.g. an English sentence) to another sequence (its Spanish translation).
concepts.significance: The machine-translation example in chapter 15 motivates the Transformer.
concepts.example: The 'sequence-to-sequence learning' entry adds 603 (PDF 627), the chapter 20 recap.
concepts.misconception: Two near-duplicate entries exist ('seq2seq …' and 'sequence-to-sequence learning'); check both.

concepts.name: Self-attention
concepts.definition: Index entry: printed 444 → PDF 468 (Transformer encoder block section).
concepts.intuition: Each token updates its representation using a weighted mix of all other tokens in the same sequence.
concepts.technical: Dot-product attention itself is introduced just before, at printed 439 (PDF 463), per the table of contents.
concepts.significance: The core mechanism of the Transformer.
concepts.example: Open PDF 468 to see self-attention used inside the encoder block.
concepts.misconception: Self-attention is not indexed at its first mention of attention; dot-product attention starts at PDF 463.

concepts.name: softmax activation
concepts.intuition: Turns a vector of scores into a probability distribution.
concepts.technical: Appears in the Reuters classifier (ch. 4), in attention scores (ch. 15) and in the chapter 20 recap.
concepts.significance: Standard last-layer activation for single-label multiclass classification.
concepts.misconception: Softmax is not only an output activation; the 440 reference is its use inside attention.
